items.stem: In Go, how does a type satisfy an interface?

options.text: Implicitly, by having the required methods; no explicit declaration is needed
options.rationale: Correct: Go uses structural typing, so any type with the interface's methods satisfies it.

options.text: By listing 'implements InterfaceName' in the type declaration
options.rationale: Go has no implements keyword; satisfaction is implicit.
Go has no class inheritance; interfaces are satisfied structurally.

options.text: By registering the type at runtime
options.rationale: No registration is needed; the compiler checks method sets.

items.explanation: Correct: Go uses structural typing, so any type with the interface's methods satisfies it.

items.stem: Which practices help avoid goroutine leaks and data races? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use context cancellation or closed channels so goroutines can exit
options.rationale: Correct: giving goroutines a way to stop prevents leaks.

options.text: Protect shared mutable state with a mutex or confine it to one goroutine
options.rationale: Correct: synchronisation or confinement prevents data races.

options.text: Share a plain map across goroutines for speed
options.rationale: Concurrent map access without synchronisation is a data race.

options.text: Launch goroutines without any way to signal them to stop
options.rationale: That is exactly how goroutines leak.

items.explanation: Correct: giving goroutines a way to stop prevents leaks.; Correct: synchronisation or confinement prevents data races.

items.stem: What is the purpose of passing a context.Context to a blocking operation?

options.text: It carries deadlines and cancellation so the operation can stop early when the caller no longer needs it
options.rationale: Correct: context propagates cancellation and deadlines across call boundaries.

options.text: It stores global configuration for the program
options.rationale: Context is for request-scoped cancellation/values, not global config.

options.text: It makes the operation run on more CPU cores
It guarantees the operation never fails
options.rationale: Context does not prevent failure; it enables cancellation.

items.explanation: Correct: context propagates cancellation and deadlines across call boundaries.
